strings.name: Anne Carson
strings.summary: Carson studied classical languages in Toronto and brought Greek literature, translation and scholarship into poetry. Autobiography of Red reworked myth, while Nox combined mourning, archives and visual form. Her writing crosses poetry, prose, essays and performance. She taught at several universities and collaborated with artists, receiving the Eliot Prize, Princess of Asturias Award and 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature. Her work joins classical reference with contemporary experience.

strings.influence.rationale: Combined classics, poetry, translation and experimental writing, extending contemporary literature’s genre boundaries through works including Autobiography of Red.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.highlights.h1.title: Reworking classical texts
strings.highlights.h1.text: Brings translation and study of ancient Greek poetry and tragedy into contemporary narrative.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Toronto BA (1974), MA (1975) and classics PhD (1981).
strings.highlights.h2.title: Writing across genres
strings.highlights.h2.text: Autobiography of Red, Nox and other works mix poetry, prose, images and archives to explore desire, memory and loss.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Nobel Prize in Literature
strings.timeline.t1.text: The Swedish Academy announced her award, recognizing writing joining classical and modern worlds and poetry with prose.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Wrong Norma published
strings.timeline.t2.text: Published a collection crossing forms, a National Book Award poetry finalist that year.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Princess of Asturias Award
strings.timeline.t3.text: Received the literature prize for writing that combines forms and traditions.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Nox published
strings.timeline.t4.text: Used an accordion book and collaged archive to mourn her brother, connecting translation and personal memory.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Eliot poetry prize
strings.timeline.t5.text: The Beauty of the Husband won the 2001 T. S. Eliot Prize.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Autobiography of Red published
strings.timeline.t6.text: Created a verse novel from an ancient Greek mythic figure, exploring identity and desire.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Eros the Bittersweet published
strings.timeline.t7.text: Examined desire in classical literature through close reading, criticism and poetic reflection.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Classics doctorate
strings.timeline.t8.text: Completed doctoral study of classical languages in Toronto, later combining teaching, translation and writing.
